chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from his father who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who says in his bowing and his prostration and his standing: "May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad", Allah would write for him the like of the bowing, and the prostration, and the standing.'

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ: May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad (a specific supplication)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Salawat during the postures of prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the immense spiritual merit of integrating salutations (Salawat) into the physical postures of Salah, a practice emphasized in Shia jurisprudence to enhance concentration (khushu). By linking the reward of each posture directly to the recitation of blessings upon the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, the Imam underscores the transformative power of dhikr in elevating the quality of obligatory worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from his father who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘The one who says in his Rukū (bowing) and his Sajdah, and his standing: ‘May Allahazwj Send Blessings upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww’, Allahazwj would Write for him (Rewards) the like of his Rukū, and his Sajdah, and the standing’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from the one whom he has mentioned from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from his father who has said the following: “

If one says during his Ruku‘, sajdah or standing position, ‘Allahumma Salli ‘Ala Muhammad wa ‘Ali Muhammad (O Allah grant Muhammad and his family a compensation worthy of their serving Your cause),’ Allah writes for him the reward for a sajdah, Ruku‘ or standing for worship.”
